::: {#sol-batch-norm-deep}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
batch_grad = first_layer_grad(make_deep(norm="batch"))
batch_loss, batch_acc = train(make_deep(norm="batch"))
print(batch_grad, batch_loss, batch_acc)
```

`r if (py$batch_loss < 0.9 * log(10)) "Yes" else "No"`.
With [batch normalization](#def-batch-norm) in every block,
the training loss after 5 [epochs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch) is `r sprintf("%.3f", py$batch_loss)`,
and the network classifies `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * py$batch_acc)`% of the test images correctly.
The [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) at the first layer has size `r sprintf("%.1e", py$batch_grad)`,
against `r sprintf("%.1e", py$plain_grad)` without it.
Each block rescales its [pre-activation](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-pre-activation)s to standard deviation about 1,
so the values do not shrink from block to block,
and neither does the gradient.

:::
